headline: The chip-industry body SEMI forecasts that spending on equipment for large chip factories in the Americas will more than double to $40.6 billion by 2029.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a useful industry forecast, but a relayed projection with no new event.
importance_line: Rising US chip-factory spending would spread chip production beyond Asia, which matters to governments and to customers who want steadier supply, but it is a forecast that depends on AI demand continuing and on companies carrying out their plans.
summary: TechNews reports, as relayed by TrendForce, that SEMI, the global semiconductor industry association, projects that spending on equipment for 300-millimetre chip factories (the standard wafer size) in the Americas, mostly in the US, will rise from $18.1 billion in 2026 to $40.6 billion in 2029 as TSMC, Intel, Micron, Samsung and Texas Instruments expand. Worldwide, SEMI expects equipment spending to grow 31% to about $149 billion in 2026 and reach $227 billion in 2029.
notes: Credit follows the chain: the TrendForce article credits TechNews for the SEMI report; the link is the TrendForce page where it was read.
